title: Cause each error on purpose
prompt:
Knowing which operation raises which exception is half the battle when reading tracebacks. Here you cause each one yourself.

Write a function `trigger(kind)` that does one ordinary operation that makes Python raise the matching built-in exception:

- `"value"` raises `ValueError`
- `"type"` raises `TypeError`
- `"zero"` raises `ZeroDivisionError`
- `"index"` raises `IndexError`
- `"key"` raises `KeyError`
- `"name"` raises `NameError`

For any other `kind`, return the string `"no error"`. Let Python raise the exception from a real mistake (like turning `"abc"` into a number); don't write `raise` yourself.
hints: Each branch needs only one line: an operation that goes wrong. Think of what you've seen fail in the lessons: converting text, mixing types, dividing, looking things up.
`int("abc")` raises `ValueError`, `"a" + 1` raises `TypeError`, and using a variable that was never assigned raises `NameError`.
An index past the end of a list raises `IndexError`; a missing key in a dictionary raises `KeyError`; dividing by `0` raises `ZeroDivisionError`.
